description:
Students at the University of Toronto, largely first-time hackathon writers. A variety of backgrounds; majors in Physics, Astrophysics, CS. Experience in machine learning, Python, Java, HTML, GIS, statistics, data science/analysis/visualization, and experimental physics. We are looking for someone with comparable experience, and eager to create a sound project - and someone looking to have fun!

Our goal is to create something that augments our research skills and is scientifically sound.
summary: T.E.R.R.A. uses satellite observations and machine learning to interpret and forecast changes in the Earth's surface. By transforming historical radar data from missions like NISAR into predictions of future ground deformation, we aim to advance Earth monitoring and support better-informed decisions in areas ranging from coastal environments to volcanic regions. This project is motivated by the goal improved emergency relief times/preparedness in the face of natural disaster.
details:
T.E.R.R.A. is a predictive Earth-observation project that combines satellite radar data from the NISAR mission with machine learning to forecast ground deformation. We process satellite observations into deformation maps and use patterns to estimate future deformation. Our initial case study focuses on volcanic deformation in Ethiopia, Peru, and Japan, but the framework can be applied to other forms of ground movement, including tectonic activity and coastal erosion.

We developed T.E.R.R.A. using Python, with tools such as ASF Search, h5py, NumPy, and Matplotlib to access, process, and visualize satellite data, alongside a machine-learning model for forecasting. What makes the project innovative is its shift from observing how Earth has changed to exploring how it might change next. Identifying patterns in ground movement, T.E.R.R.A. could provide researchers with another tool for studying changing landscapes and assessing potential risks. We considered factors such as data quality, measurement uncertainty, model accuracy, and whether the approach could work across different regions. Our long-term goal is to make satellite observations more predictive and help us better understand our changing planet.
